t: This is the equestrian statue of Edward VII, a Grade II listed monument on Waterloo Place, just north of the Duke of York Column. A statue of Robert Napier stood on this spot from 1891 before it. Edward VII was King from 1901 until 1910. The sculptor was Sir Bertram Mackennal, the first Australian to be elected an Associate of the Royal Academy and the first Australian artist to be knighted. The monument was designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens, whom the historian Gavin Stamp called surely the greatest British architect of the twentieth century.
